name: Tessera TK-7 Service Pistol 'Ticker'
description:
The Tessera TK-7 is a striker-fired semi-automatic pistol chambered in 9x19mm, issued as the standard sidearm to Tessera Corponation's security and administrative enforcement divisions. The weapon features a proprietary biometric grip that locks the firing mechanism unless the registered user's palm print is detected — a feature Tessera markets as 'personnel security' but which critics note also prevents anyone from testifying about the weapon's performance by firing it themselves.

The TK-7 is a competent but unremarkable pistol elevated by its Tessera branding and biometric lock system. Build quality is good, accuracy is acceptable, and the trigger has the slightly mushy character common to striker-fired designs. The biometric system adds 0.2 seconds to the first shot — a delay that has been the subject of multiple internal review boards after field incidents.

Every Tessera facility in GLMZ has racks of TK-7s in its security office. The weapon is so associated with the corponation that carrying one outside Tessera employment is considered a social signal — either you're a former Tessera employee, or you want people to think you are.
specifications:
caliber: 9x19mm
effective_range: 50 meters
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 15 rounds
weight: 0.71 kg
tactical_use: Standard duty sidearm with biometric user authentication. Reliable in normal conditions but the biometric lock introduces a slight first-shot delay. Ineffective if the registered user is incapacitated, as the weapon cannot be picked up and used by allies. Tessera security teams train extensively to mitigate the delay through pre-engagement grip protocols.
cultural_context: The TK-7 is Tessera's corporate identity rendered in polymer and steel. Carrying one announces corponation affiliation more loudly than a badge. Former Tessera employees sometimes keep their issued TK-7s as severance souvenirs — technically illegal, universally tolerated.
known_users: Black market buyers seeking biometric bypass models
story_hooks: A TK-7 with its biometric lock disabled fires in a crowd — and the ballistics match a weapon that was supposed to be locked in a Tessera evidence vault.
Someone is selling a biometric bypass chip for TK-7s on the Shelf black market, and Tessera wants it suppressed before the media finds out.

physical_description.visual_profile: A clean, corporate-aesthetic striker-fired pistol with aggressive geometry softened by premium finishing. The grip module features a prominent biometric sensor panel that catches light distinctively. Angular, purposeful lines suggest both military heritage and boardroom polish. Unmistakably a tier-2 corporate issue weapon.
physical_description.dimensions: 18.5cm overall length, 12.8cm grip height, 3.2cm slide width. 10.2cm barrel length.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and controllable in-hand despite the polymer frame. Feels substantial without being fatiguing — designed for extended duty wear. The biometric module adds tactile weight to the grip.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer frame with hardened steel slide. The biometric sensor housing is a composite material with embedded conductive elements.
physical_description.finish: Satin-brushed steel slide contrasting with matte charcoal polymer frame. The biometric grip panel has a subtle metallic sheen under direct light, suggesting embedded circuitry.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey slide, midnight charcoal frame, with accent lighting in the biometric sensor housing that cycles blue when active. Tessera corporate silver trim on the trigger guard.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured polymer grip with embedded sensor surface — not quite rubberized, more like finely-grooved industrial composite. The biometric panel feels smooth, slightly warm to touch.
distinctive_features: Prominent biometric sensor plate on grip — rectangular, with subtle LED indicators
Tessera Media Group corporate logo laser-etched on slide in silver
Serial number plate integrated into trigger guard
Textured vertical grip serrations fore and aft of trigger guard
Recessed optics rail on slide — pre-drilled for sights
Magazine release button marked with Φ currency symbol
Small status light in grip that illuminates when biometric lock engages
Wear marks typically visible on biometric sensor from heavy duty use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Media Group logo prominently etched on slide in corporate silver, positioned above rear sight. 'TK-7 SERVICE PISTOL' stamped along the frame rail. Serial number and manufacturing date on left side of trigger guard. Caliber marking 9x19mm on barrel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Exceptionally well-maintained in active service — Tessera issues replacements on wear cycles. Biometric sensor panel shows accumulated fingerprint oils and faint wear from thousands of authentication attempts. Occasionally seen with micro-scratches on slide finish from duty holster contact. Never truly battle-worn; Tessera replaces damaged units rather than field-repair.
